meaning: A work works if it draws the 874 bridges faithfully to the record (positions in Delaware's real shape, years, lengths, traffic, ratings, counts and annotations all true to the CSV) and reads legibly, with no wrong facts, broken encodings or collided labels.

items.why: The map loses Delaware's shape (bridges spread over a rectangle), and the county labels and the longest-bridge note pile on top of each other.
The map arches are coloured wrongly: under half of the isolated bridges match their rating, and the rating-4 C&D Canal bridge is drawn in the rating-3 red.
The note on the longest bridge (3,291 m, 1951) says it carries 'Sr1/Korean War Vet Mem' over nothing named, but that bridge crosses the Delaware River carrying I 295/US 40.
The map positions, colours, rating counts (41/335/374/114/7/3), 1965-69 peak of 88 and the Delaware River 3,291 m 1951 note all match the data, and the work reads clearly.
The map's bridge positions are distorted into a rectangle that is not Delaware, so 'each drawn where it stands' is false.
The map's positions are wrong (only about 560 of 874 bridges land where they really stand), so the state's shape is lost.
It names the longest bridge 'Mispillion River, 1939', which is false, its county labels are printed on top of each other, and the map positions are wrong.
The stroke weight does not follow traffic as its caption claims: roads with 44 vehicles a day are drawn as heavy as ones with 18,000.
The arch widths do not follow length: the 44 m 1839 bridge is drawn wide, while the 2,570 m C&D Canal bridge is tiny.
The latitudes, years, length widths (the C&D Canal spans show up as the large arches), colours and the ten rated-poor dots all match the record.
The map scatters the bridges over a featureless rectangle that is not Delaware's real geography.

The 'where' panel is scrambled: the county labels are out of order and crowded together, and the bridges sit at the wrong latitudes (for example, the 1942 rated-poor dot falls near 39°15' instead of 39°43').
The ratings are coloured wrongly: the rating-5 Delaware River bridge and the rating-4 C&D Canal bridge are drawn in the good-condition blues.
The 'where' map misplaces most bridges (Delaware's shape is lost, and the rated-poor dots disagree with the year panel).
The positions, length widths, traffic weights and rating colours all agree with the record, and the year histogram and labels are correct and legible.
The map has Delaware's true shape with correct rating colours, and the legend counts and the oldest bridge (1839, Brandywine Creek) are right.
The map is distorted out of Delaware's shape, the three county labels overprint one another, and the Delaware River leader line points to the wrong place.
It says the oldest bridge crosses 'sr 1 milford bypass' (it crosses Brandywine Creek), and its map is not Delaware's shape.
The map's bridge positions are scrambled into a rectangle, so it does not show where the bridges stand.
The rated-poor dots are on the wrong bridges, including one on a bridge built around 2018, when no poor-rated bridge is newer than 1977.
